title: Constitution of Bangladesh
content:
{{Short description|Supreme law of Bangladesh}} {{Use Bangladeshi English|date=July 2021}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2013}} {{Infobox constitution | document_name= Constitution of Bangladesh | image = বাংলাদেশের সংবিধান ১৯৭২ (পৃষ্ঠা ১).jpg | image_size= | image_caption= First page of the original Constitution of Bangladesh in Bangla | date_ratified= {{Start date and age|df=yes|1972|11|04}} | date_effective= {{Start date and age|df=yes|1972|12|16}} | writer= [[Kamal Hossain|Dr Kamal Hossain]]
{{small|Chairman of the Constitution Drafting Committee}} and other members of [[Constituent Assembly of Bangladesh|Constituent Assembly]] | signers= 404 members of the [[Constituent Assembly of Bangladesh]] | system = [[Unitary state|Unitary]] [[Parliamentary]] [[Constitutional Republic]] | date_last_amended = 8 July 2018 | citation = {{citation |url= http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-details-367.html |title= Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh |date= 2021-06-13}} | federalism = No | chambers = [[Jatiya Sangsad|One]] | branches = Three (Executive, Legislature and Judiciary) | executive = [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Prime Minister]] and cabinet responsible to the [[Jatiya Sangsad]] | jurisdiction = {{flag|Bangladesh}} | courts = [[Supreme Court of Bangladesh|Supreme Court]] | number_amendments = [[Amendments to the Constitution of Bangladesh|17]] | electoral_college = No | supersedes = [[Proclamation of Bangladeshi Independence]] | location_of_document = [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]] }} {{Politics of Bangladesh}} The '''Constitution of Bangladesh''' ({{lang-bn|বাংলাদেশের সংবিধান}} — {{transl|bn|''Bangladesher Sambidhāna''}}), officially the '''Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh''' ({{lang-bn|গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশের সংবিধান}} — {{transl|bn|''Gaṇaprajātantrī Bangladesher Sambidhāna''}}) is the supreme [[law of Bangladesh]]. The document provides the framework that demarcates the Bangladeshi republic with a [[unitary state|unitary]], [[Parliamentary system|parliamentary democracy]], that enshrines fundamental [[human rights]] and [[freedoms]], an [[Judiciary of Bangladesh|independent judiciary]], [[Local government in Bangladesh|democratic local government]] and a [[Bangladesh Civil Service|national bureaucracy]]. The four fundamental principles of the Constitution are [[Bengali nationalism|nationalism]],{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24557.html|title=Article 9 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-29|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} [[Socialism in Bangladesh|socialism]],{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24558.html|title=Article 10 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-29|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} [[Democracy in Bangladesh|democracy]]{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24559.html|title=Article 11 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-29|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} and [[Secularism in Bangladesh|secularism]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24560.html|title=Article 12 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-29|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} The Constitution endeavors to create a [[Socialist state|socialist society]] in which the [[rule of law]], fundamental [[human rights]] and [[freedom]], [[Social equality|equality]] and [[justice]], [[Social justice|political, economic and social]], is secured for all its citizens. It commits Bangladesh to “contribute to [[World peace|international peace]] and co-operation in keeping with the [[Progressivism|progressive]] aspirations of mankind”.{{cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367.html |title=Preamble of the Constitution of Bangladesh |publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]|access-date=2021-06-18}}{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24556.html|title=Article 8 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-29|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} It invokes constitutional supremacy, as opposed to [[legislative supremacy]] since it was created by a [[Constituent Assembly of Bangladesh|constituent assembly]] not [[Jatiya Sangsad|Parliament]] and was adopted by the people of Bangladesh in its preamble. Parliament cannot [[Ouster clause|quash parts of the Constitution]]. [[Judicial precedent]] is enshrined in Bangladesh's Constitution under Article 111,{{cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24668.html |title=Article 111 of the Constitution of Bangladesh |access-date=2021-06-18}} which makes Bangladesh an integral part of the [[common law]] world. [[Judicial review in Bangladesh|Judicial review]] is also supported by the Constitution. It was adopted by the [[Constituent Assembly of Bangladesh]] on 4 November 1972 and became effective on 16 December 1972. The Constitution replaced the [[Proclamation of Bangladeshi Independence|Proclamation of Independence]] as the country's fundamental instrument of government. The Constitution became effective on Bangladesh's [[Victory Day (Bangladesh)|Victory Day]], precisely one year after the signing of the [[Pakistani Instrument of Surrender|Instrument of Surrender]]. The constitution has been [[Amendments to the Constitution of Bangladesh|amended 17 times]] since its adoption, a two-thirds [[supermajority]] is required in the Jatiya Sangsad to secure a constitutional amendment. ==Modern Constitutional history== ===British India=== The [[Company Raj|advent of British rule]] in the 18th century displaced the centuries of governance developed by South Asian empires. The [[Regulating Act of 1773]] passed by the [[Parliament of the United Kingdom]] was the first basic law in the [[Bengal Presidency]]. The [[British Empire]] did not grant universal suffrage and democratic institutions to its colonies. The British slowly granted concessions for home rule. The [[Government of India Act 1858]], [[Indian Councils Act 1861]], [[Indian Councils Act 1892]] and [[Indian Councils Act 1909]] were later important laws of government. The [[legislatures of British India]] included the [[Bengal Legislative Council]] and the [[Eastern Bengal and Assam Legislative Council]] in the early 20th century. The [[Nehru Report]] recommended for universal suffrage, a bicameral legislature, a senate and a house of representatives. The [[Fourteen Points of Jinnah]] demanded provincial autonomy and quotas for Muslims in government. The [[Government of India Act 1935]] established provincial parliaments based on separate electorates.{{cite web |url=http://en.banglapedia.org/index.php?title=Constitutional_Development |title=Constitutional Development |website=Banglapedia |access-date=2017-07-11}} The 1940 [[Lahore Resolution]], supported by the first [[Prime Minister of Bengal]], asked the British government that "the North Western and Eastern Zones of (British) India should be grouped to constitute ‘independent states’". It further proclaimed "that adequate, effective and mandatory safeguards should be specifically provided in the Constitution for minorities in these units and in the regions for the protection of their religious, cultural, economic, political, administrative and other rights". The resolution's status is akin to the magna carta in [[Pakistan]], in terms of the concept of independence.{{cite book|author1=Mahendra Prasad Singh|author2=Veena Kukreja|title=Federalism in South Asia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s3g9BAAAQBAJ&pg=PA92|date=7 August 2014|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-317-55973-3|page=92}}{{cite book|author=Ayesha Jalal|title=Democracy and Authoritarianism in South Asia: A Comparative and Historical Perspective|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mHPok4epvlIC&pg=PA184|date=6 April 1995|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-47862-5|page=184}}{{cite book|author1=Mark Tushnet|author2=Madhav Khosla|title=Unstable Constitutionalism|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ojMZCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA142|date=17 September 2015|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-1-107-06895-7|page=142}} On 20 June 1947, the [[Bengal Legislative Assembly]] voted on the [[Partition of Bengal (1947)|partition of Bengal]]. It was decided by 120 votes to 90 that, if Bengal remained united, it should join the [[Constituent Assembly of Pakistan]]. At a separate meeting of legislators from West Bengal, it was decided by 58 votes to 21 that the province should be partitioned and that West Bengal should join the [[Constituent Assembly of India]]. At another separate meeting of legislators from East Bengal, it was decided by 106 votes to 35 that Bengal should not be partitioned and 107 votes to 34 that East Bengal should join the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan if Bengal was partitioned.{{cite book|author=Soumyendra Nath Mukherjee|title=Sir William Jones: A Study in Eighteenth-century British Attitudes to India|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Bhd-_1RE04MC&pg=PA230|year=1987|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-86131-581-9|page=230}} On 6 July 1947, the [[1947 Sylhet referendum|Sylhet referendum]] voted to partition [[Sylhet Division]] from [[Assam Province]] and merge it into East Bengal. On 11 August 1947, [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]], the president of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, declared that religious minorities would enjoy full freedom of religion in the emergent new state.{{Cite web|url=http://www.columbia.edu/itc/mealac/pritchett/00islamlinks/txt_jinnah_assembly_1947.html|title=Mr. Jinnah's address to the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan|publisher=Columbia University |access-date=2019-08-15}} ===Union with Pakistan=== Section 8 of the [[Indian Independence Act 1947]] provided that the Government of India Act, 1935 with certain amendments and adaptations would be the working Constitution of the [[Dominion of Pakistan]] during the transitional period. The Constituent Assembly of Pakistan included 79 members, of whom 44 were from [[East Bengal]], 22 from West Punjab, 5 from Sind, 3 from the North West Frontier Province, 1 from Baluchistan and 4 from the acceding princely states. The [[Bengali Language Movement]] and demands for replacing separate electorates with joint universal suffrage were key issues in East Bengal. The first constituent assembly was arbitrarily dissolved by the Governor General in 1954. This led to the court challenge of ''[[Federation of Pakistan v. Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan]]'', in which the federal court supported the Governor General's decision, although Justice [[A. R. Cornelius]] expressed dissent. The dissolution of the assembly was one of the first major blows to democracy in Pakistan. The [[Constitution of Pakistan of 1956]] was adopted by a second constituent assembly elected in 1955. It declared two provinces- [[East Pakistan]] and [[West Pakistan]]; and two federal languages- [[Urdu]] and [[Bengali language|Bengali]]. The first Pakistani Constitution was in place for only a few years. General Ayub Khan staged a military coup and introduced the [[Constitution of Pakistan of 1962]]. The 1962 Constitution introduced a [[presidential system]] in which [[electoral college]]s would be responsible for electing the president and governors. The chief ministers' offices were abolished; and parliament and provincial assemblies were delegated to a mainly advisory role. The system was dubbed "Basic Democracy". In 1965, [[Fatima Jinnah]]'s failed bid for the presidency prompted allegations of a rigged electoral system. The [[Six point movement|Six Points of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]] demanded parliamentary democracy. Rahman's Six Points were part of the manifesto of the Awami League, the party which won first general election in East and West Pakistan in 1970. The Awami League ran on the platform of developing a new Pakistani Constitution based on the Six Points. The League won 167 out 169 East Pakistani seats in the [[National Assembly of Pakistan]] and 288 out of 300 seats in the [[East Pakistan Provincial Assembly]]. The Pakistani military junta refused to transfer power to [[Prime Minister-elect]] Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, and instead executed [[Operation Searchlight]] which triggered [[Bangladesh War of Independence]]. ===Bangladesh=== The [[Provisional Government of Bangladesh]] issued the [[Proclamation of Bangladeshi Independence|Proclamation of Independence]] on 10 April 1971, which served as the interim first Constitution of Bangladesh. It declared “equality, human dignity and social justice” as the fundamental principles of the republic. East Pakistani members of Pakistan's federal and provincial assemblies were transformed into members of the [[Constituent Assembly of Bangladesh]]. The constituent assembly had 404 members. After the war, the Constitution Drafting Committee was formed in 1972. The committee included 34 members with Dr. [[Kamal Hossain]] as its chairman. The Constitution Bill was introduced in the Assembly on 12 October. Its first reading began on 19 October and continued till 30 October. The second reading took place from 31 October to 3 November. [[Manabendra Narayan Larma]] made an impassioned appeal to declare the term of citizenship as “Bangladeshi” instead of “[[Bengali people|Bengali]]”.{{cite news |author=Hana Shams Ahmed |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-153616 |title=Our Constitution |newspaper=The Daily Star |access-date=2017-07-11}} Larma argued that labeling all citizens as Bengali discriminated against non-Bengali communities, including his own [[Chakma people|Chakma]] ethnic group. The third reading began on 4 November and it approved 65 amendments to the Constitution Bill and adopted and enacted the Constitution on 4 November. The Constitution came into effect on 16 December 1972. A [[Westminster system|Westminster style]] political system was established. It declared nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism as the fundamental principles of the republic. It proclaimed fundamental human rights, including [[freedom of speech]], [[freedom of religion]], [[freedom of movement]], [[freedom of assembly]], the [[right to education]] and public healthcare among others. A two thirds vote of parliament was required to amend the Constitution. After winning the 1973 general election, the Awami League government often flouted Constitutional rules and principles. The government received strong criticism from the Bangladeshi press, including both Bengali and English newspapers. The [[Committee for Civil Liberties and Legal Aid]] was formed to defend the Constitution. The Awami League enacted three Constitutional amendments between 1973 and 1975. The most drastic amendment was in January 1975. It introduced a one party state and a presidential government, while the judiciary's independence was greatly curtailed. Constitutional rule was suspended on 15 August 1975 with the assassination of President Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and the declaration of [[martial law]]. The [[Chief Martial Law Administrator]] issued a series of Proclamation Orders between 1975 and 1979 which amended the Constitution. Lieutenant General Ziaur Rahman is credited for many of these Proclamation Orders. The most significant of these orders was defining citizenship as [[Bangladeshi]]; other orders included the insertion of religious references and the controversial [[Indemnity Act, Bangladesh|Indemnity Ordinance]]. In 1979, martial law was lifted, [[multiparty]] politics was restored and Constitutional rule was revived. The Fifth Amendment in 1979 validated all Proclamation Orders of the martial law authorities. An executive presidency continued until 1982. Martial law was again imposed in the [[1982 Bangladesh coup d'état]]. When Constitutional rule was restored in 1986, the Sixth Amendment validated previous Proclamation Orders issued by the Chief Martial Law Administrator. The Eighth Amendment in 1988 declared Islam as the [[state religion]] and initiated limited devolution of the judiciary. In 1990, a pro-democracy uprising ousted President Ershad. The uprising was followed by parliamentary elections in 1991. The Twelfth Amendment passed by the fifth parliament is the most influential Constitutional amendment in Bangladesh. It re-established parliamentary government. It amended Articles 48, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 70, 72, 109, 119, 124, 141A and 142. The Prime Minister became the executive head of government, and along with the cabinet, was responsible to parliament. Local government was made more democratic. However, the amendment restricted the voting freedom of MPs. According to Article 70, MPs would lose their seat if they voted against their party. This made it impossible for parliament to have a free vote, including no-confidence motions to remove a prime minister. Experts have described the amendment as instituting prime ministerial dictatorship. The Thirteen Amendment in 1996 introduced the [[Caretaker government of Bangladesh]]. In 2010, the [[Supreme Court of Bangladesh]] ruled that the Fifth Amendment of 1979 went against the Constitutional spirit of the country and hence invalidated its removal of clauses related to secularism. The Supreme Court gave the verdict in the case of ''[[Bangladesh Italian Marble Works Ltd. v. Government of Bangladesh]]''. While implementing the supreme court's verdict in the Fifteenth Amendment in 2011, the Awami League-led parliament abolished the caretaker government system, which the party itself had advocated in 1996. In 2017, the Supreme Court declared the Sixteenth Amendment Act of 2014 illegal and void. The amendment had introduced the provision of impeaching judges in parliament. The Supreme Court held that parliament cannot have [[conscience vote]]s due to [[Article 70 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|Article 70]].{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/editorial/16th-amendment-scrapped-1427797 |title=16th Amendment scrapped |work=The Daily Star |date=2017-07-04 |type=Editorial |access-date=2017-07-11}} ==Contents== ===Preamble===
'''BISMILLAH-AR-RAHMAN-AR-RAHIM'''
In the name of Allah, the Beneficient, the Merciful
In the name of the Creator, the Merciful. We, the people of Bangladesh, having proclaimed our independence on the 26th day of March, 1971 and through a historic struggle for national liberation, established the independent, sovereign People's Republic of Bangladesh; Pledging that the high ideals of nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism, which inspired our heroic people to dedicate themselves to, and our brave martyrs to sacrifice their lives in, the national liberation struggle, shall be the fundamental principles of the Constitution; Further pledging that it shall be a fundamental aim of the State to realise through the democratic process a socialist society, free from exploitation a society in which the rule of law, fundamental human rights and freedom, equality and justice, political, economic and social, will be secured for all citizens; Affirming that it is our sacred duty to safeguard, protect and defend this Constitution and to maintain its supremacy as the embodiment of the will of the people of Bangladesh so that we may prosper in freedom and may make our full contribution towards international peace and co operation in keeping with the progressive aspirations of mankind; In our Constituent Assembly, this eighteenth day of Kartick, 1379 B.S., corresponding to the fourth day of November, 1972 A.D., do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution.
===The Constitution=== ===Part I: The Republic=== States that Bangladesh is a unitary republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24547.html|title=Article 1 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Demarcates the territory of the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24548.html|title=Article 2 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Proclaims that [[Islam]] is the state religion, but guarantees equal status and equal rights to all religions.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24549.html|title=Article 2A of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Declares [[Bengali language|Bangla]] as the state language.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24550.html|title=Article 3 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the [[Amar Sonar Bangla|national anthem]], [[Flag of Bangladesh|national flag]], and [[National Emblem of Bangladesh|national emblem]] of the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24551.html|title=Article 4 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Declares [[Dhaka]] as the [[national capital]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24553.html|title=Article 5 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Provides eligibility for citizenship.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24554.html|title=Article 6 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that all powers are derived from the people, and the exercise of such powers will be by the authority of the Constitution. Proclaims that the Constitution is the supreme law of Bangladesh, and that any laws inconsistent with the Constitution are void and of no effect.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24555.html|title=Article 7 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Article 7A prohibits the suspension or abrogation of the Constitution.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-41503.html|title=Article 7A of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that certain parts of the Constitution are unamendable.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-41504.html|title=Article 7B of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-28|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ===Part II: Fundamental Principles of State Policy=== States that [[Bengali nationalism|nationalism]], [[socialism]], [[democracy]] and [[secularism]] are the fundamental principles of state policy. Pledges to ensure the emancipation of peasants and workers.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24562.html|title=Article 14 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that education will be free and compulsory.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24565.html|title=Article 17 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Endeavours to protect and improve the environment.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-41505.html|title=Article 18A of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Republic will ensure equality of opportunity to all citizens. States that endeavours will be made to ensure the equality of opportunity and participation of women in all spheres of life.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24567.html|title=Article 19 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Declares the [[separation of powers]] between the judiciary and the executive.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24570.html|title=Article 22 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that measures will be adopted to conserve cultural traditions and the heritage of the people.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24571.html|title=Article 23 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}}{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-41506.html|title=Article 23A of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Ensures the protection of national monuments.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24572.html|title=Article 24 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Republic will promote international peace and to support oppressed people throughout the world.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24573.html|title=Article 25 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-06-30|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ===Part III: Fundamental Rights=== {{see also|Fundamental rights in Bangladesh}} Declares that all laws inconsistent with the fundamental rights of the Constitution are to be void.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24574.html|title=Article 26 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Enshrines the principle of equality before the law.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24575.html|title=Article 27 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prohibits discrimination on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24576.html|title=Article 28 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that there will be equality of opportunity for people who seek public employment.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24577.html|title=Article 29 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prohibits citizens of the Republic from receiving foreign titles, honours, awards or decorations without prior approval by the President.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24578.html|title=Article 30 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Declares that the protection of the law is the inalienable right of all citizens.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24579.html|title=Article 31 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Proclaims that no person shall be deprived of life and personal liberty.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24580.html|title=Article 32 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Provides safeguards for those in detention.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24580.html|title=Article 33 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prohibits the use of forced labour.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24582.html|title=Article 34 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Provides protections for persons in respect of trial and punishment.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24582.html|title=Article 35 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Enshrines freedom of movement;{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24584.html|title=Article 36 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} freedom of assembly;{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24585.html|title=Article 37 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} freedom of association;{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24586.html|title=Article 38 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} freedom of thought, conscience and speech;{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24587.html|title=Article 39 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} freedom of profession or occupation;{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24588.html|title=Article 40 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} and freedom of religion.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24589.html|title=Article 41 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that all citizens have the right to acquire property.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24590.html|title=Article 42 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that all citizens have the right to protect their homes and means of communication.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24591.html|title=Article 43 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Declares that the Supreme Court will enforce the fundamental rights of the Constitution.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24592.html|title=Article 44 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Reserves the right to provide indemnity to individuals.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24593.html|title=Article 46 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-04|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} === Part IV: The Executive === ==== Chapter I: The President ==== {{see also|President of Bangladesh}} Declares that Bangladesh will have a [[President of Bangladesh|President]] who will serve as [[Head of state|Head of State]] of the Republic. States that the President will be elected by members of the [[Jatiya Sangsad]]. Prescribes that the President will only act in accordance with the advice of the Prime Minister, with the exception of the appointment of the [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Prime Minister]] and the [[Chief Justice of Bangladesh|Chief Justice]]. Specifies that the President must have attained the age of 35 years, and must be qualified for election as a Member of Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24597.html|title=Article 48 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the President has the power to grant [[pardon]]s and to commute or suspend the sentences of individuals convicted in a court.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24598.html|title=Article 49 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies that the President is limited to serving two 5-year terms in office, regardless of whether they are consecutive or not. Outlines that in order to tender their resignation, the President must write under their hand addressed to the [[Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad|Speaker]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24599.html|title=Article 50 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the process of impeachment and removal from office of the President.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24601.html|title=Article 52 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the process of removal from office of the President on grounds of physical or mental incapacity.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24602.html|title=Article 53 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Speaker will discharge the duties of President in the event of the President's absence.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24603.html|title=Article 54 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter II: The Prime Minister and The Cabinet ==== {{see also|Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Cabinet of Bangladesh}} States that the Republic is to have a [[Cabinet of Bangladesh|Cabinet]] with the [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Prime Minister]] as its [[Head of government|Head]]. Prescribes that the executive power of the Republic is to be exercised by or on the authority of the Prime Minister.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24604.html|title=Article 56 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that appointments to the Cabinet will be determined by the Prime Minister and made by the [[President of Bangladesh|President]]. Specifies that not less than nine-tenths of members of the Cabinet must be Members of Parliament. States that the President will appoint as Prime Minister the Member of Parliament who appears to command the confidence of the [[Jatiya Sangsad]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24605.html|title=Article 56 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the office of Prime Minister will become vacant in the event they: tender their resignation to the President; cease to be a Member of Parliament or cease to retain the confidence of the majority of members of the [[Jatiya Sangsad]]. There are no term limits specified for the Prime Minister.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24606.html|title=Article 57 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the tenure of office of other Ministers.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24607.html|title=Article 58 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter III: Local Government ==== {{see also|Local government in Bangladesh}} Makes provision for democratically-elected local government in every administrative unit in the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24613.html|title=Article 59 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that powers exercised by local government will be delegated by [[Jatiya Sangsad|Parliament]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24614.html|title=Article 60 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter IV: The Defence Services ==== {{see also|Armed Forces of Bangladesh}} Declares that the [[President of Bangladesh|President]] is the [[Commander-in-chief|Commander-in-Chief]] of the [[Armed Forces of Bangladesh]]. States that the exercise of such powers will be determined by law.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24615.html|title=Article 61 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Parliament will by law provide for the regulation of the defence services, including the maintenance of the defence services; the grating of commissions; the appointment of chiefs of staff of the defence services and the discipline and other matters relating to the defence services.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24616.html|title=Article 62 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Reserves the right to [[Declaration of war|declare war]] for Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24617.html|title=Article 63 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-05|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter V: The Attorney General ==== {{see also|Attorney General of Bangladesh}} States that the [[President of Bangladesh|President]] will appoint someone who is qualified to serve as a Justice of the [[Supreme Court of Bangladesh|Supreme Court]] as [[Attorney General of Bangladesh|Attorney General]]. States that in exercise of their duties, the Attorney General is entitled to attend the proceedings of any courts in the Republic. === Part V: The Legislature === ==== Chapter I: Parliament ==== {{see also|Jatiya Sangsad|Member of Parliament (Bangladesh)}} Proclaims that there will be a Parliament for Bangladesh known as the House of the Nation, which will be vested with the legislative powers of the Republic. States that Parliament will consist of 300 directly-elected members, while 50 seats will be reserved exclusively for women and will be allocated on a [[Proportional representation|proportional basis]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24619.html|title=Article 65 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies that a person is required to be a citizen of Bangladesh who has attained the age of 25 years in order to qualify for election to Parliament. Also specifies the procedure to disqualify an individual from election to Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24620.html|title=Article 66 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the procedure for a Member of Parliament to vacate their seat. States that a Member of Parliament who is absent from Parliament for 90 consecutive days will of vacated their seat.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24621.html|title=Article 67 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Members of Parliament are entitled to remuneration.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24622.html|title=Article 68 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prescribes a penalty for Members of Parliament who take their seats or vote before reciting the [[oath of office]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24623.html|title=Article 69 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that a Member of Parliament who resigns from their party or votes against their party in Parliament will vacate their seat.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24624.html|title=Article 70 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Allows candidates to stand for election in multiple constituencies, but in the event a single candidate is elected to more than one, they are required to vacate all but one seat.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24625.html|title=Article 71 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies that Parliament will be summoned, prorogued and dissolved by the President. States that Parliament will sit for a five-year term.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24626.html|title=Article 72 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Decrees that at the commencement of the first session of Parliament after a general election and the commencement of the first session of Parliament every year, the President is to make an address to Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24627.html|title=Article 73 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Ministers are entitled to address and take part in the proceedings of Parliament, but only Minister who are Members of Parliament are entitled to vote.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24628.html|title=Article 73A of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Parliament will, in its first sitting after a general election, elect a [[Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad|Speaker]] and Deputy Speaker among its members.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24629.html|title=Article 74 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the individual presiding over proceedings is not entitled to vote unless there is an equality of votes. Specifies that the [[quorum]] of the Parliament will be 60 members.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24630.html|title=Article 75 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Parliament will appoint among its members a number of standing committees.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24631.html|title=Article 76 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Makes provision for the establishment of the office of the Ombudsman.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24632.html|title=Article 77 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Members of Parliament are protected by [[parliamentary privilege]]. Prescribes that Parliament will have its own secretariat.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24634.html|title=Article 79 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-06|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter II: Legislative and Financial Procedures ==== Outlines the [[Parliamentary procedure|legislative procedure]] for a [[Bill (law)|Bill]] to become an [[Act of Parliament]]. States that assent is required from the [[President of Bangladesh|President]] in order for a Bill to become an Act of Parliament. Specifies that if the President fails to assent to a Bill within fifteen days of it being presented to them, it will be deemed that they have assented to the bill and it will become law.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24636.html|title=Article 80 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the legislative procedure for [[Money bill|Money Bills]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24637.html|title=Article 81 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Money Bills can only be introduced with the recommendation of the President.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24638.html|title=Article 82 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that taxes can only be levied or collected under the authority of an Act of Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24639.html|title=Article 84 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that taxes can only be levied and collected under the authority of an Act of Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24639.html|title=Article 83 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that all revenue received by the [[Government of Bangladesh|Government]] from the repayment of loans will form part of a single fund known as the Consolidated Fund. States that all other public revenue will be credited to the Public Account of the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24640.html|title=Article 84 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the custody of public money and their payment into and the withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund will be regulated by an Act of Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24641.html|title=Article 85 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the revenue payable to the Public Account of the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24642.html|title=Article 86 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that an [[Budget|Annual Financial Statement]] must be laid before Parliament for each respective [[Fiscal year|financial year]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24643.html|title=Article 87 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the charges of the Consolidated Fund.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24644.html|title=Article 88 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the procedure relating to the Annual Financial Statement.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24645.html|title=Article 89 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Makes provision for an Appropriations Act to be defrayed from the Consolidated Fund.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24646.html|title=Article 90 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Makes provision for the use of supplementary and excess grants, in the event the total amount authorised to spend in a fiscal year is not sufficient.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24647.html|title=Article 91 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the powers of Parliament in relation to the Consolidated Fund.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24648.html|title=Article 92 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-07|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter III: Ordinance Making Power ==== States that in the event that the [[Jatiya Sangsad]] is dissolved, and immediate action is necessary, the [[President of Bangladesh|President]] may make or promulgate Ordinances. === Part VI: The Judiciary === ==== Chapter I: The Supreme Court ==== {{see also| Supreme Court of Bangladesh}} Declares that there is to be a [[Supreme court|Supreme Court]], consisting of an [[Bangladesh Supreme Court, Appellate Division|Appellate Division]] and a [[High Court Division]]. States that there is to be a [[Chief Justice of Bangladesh|Chief Justice]] and other Judges who are to be appointed by the [[President of Bangladesh|President]]. Decrees that the Chief Justice and the other Judges will be [[Judicial independence|independent]] in the exercise of their judicial functions.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24651.html|title=Article 94 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the procedure for the appointment of the Chief Justice and other Judges. States that a Judge must be a citizen of Bangladesh who has either been an Advocate at the Supreme Court for a minimum of ten years, or has held judicial office in Bangladesh for ten years.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24652.html|title=Article 95 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that a Judge is entitled to serve until they have attained the age of sixty-seven years. States that the President can, pursuant to a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds of Members of Parliament, remove Judges.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24653.html|title=Article 96 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Makes provision for the temporary appointment of the Chief Justice.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24654.html|title=Article 97 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the President may appoint one or more duly qualified persons to serve as an Additional Judge for a period not exceeding two years.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24655.html|title=Article 98 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that after their retirement or removal, a Judge is prohibited from holding an office of profit in service of the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24656.html|title=Article 99 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the seat of the Supreme Court will be the national capital, [[Dhaka]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24657.html|title=Article 100 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the [[jurisdiction]] of the High Court Division.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24658.html|title=Article 101 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Grants the High Court Division the authority to issue certain orders and directions.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24658.html|title=Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the jurisdiction of the Appellate Division.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24660.html|title=Article 103 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Grants the Appellate Division the power to issue directions, orders, decrees or writs.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24661.html|title=Article 104 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Appellate Division will have the power to review any judgments or orders issued by it.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24662.html|title=Article 105 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that in the event that the President believes a question of law has arisen that is of public importance, the Supreme Court may report its opinion to the President.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24663.html|title=Article 106 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Supreme Court has the power to make rules which regulate the practise and procedure of each Division of the Supreme Court and any other subordinate court.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24664.html|title=Article 107 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Supreme Court will be a [[court of record]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24665.html|title=Article 108 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Supreme Court will have superintendence over all courts and tribunals subordinate to it.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24666.html|title=Article 109 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the procedure for the transfer of cases from subordinate courts to the High Court Division.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24667.html|title=Article 110 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the law declared by the Appellate Division and the High Court Division will be legally-binding and will be binding in all subordinate courts in the Republic. States that all authorities, executive and judicial, in the Republic will act in aid of the Supreme Court.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24669.html|title=Article 112 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the appointment procedure of the staff of the Supreme Court.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24670.html|title=Article 113 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter II: Subordinate Courts ==== {{see also|Judiciary of Bangladesh}} Makes provision for the establishment of subordinate courts in the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24671.html|title=Article 114 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines that the appointment of persons to offices in the judicial service or as magistrates exercising judicial functions will be made by the President.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24672.html|title=Article 115 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the control and discipline of subordinate courts will be vested in the President and will be exercised in consultation with the Supreme Court.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24673.html|title=Article 116 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that all persons employed in the judicial service and all magistrates shall be [[Judicial independence|independent]] in the exercise of their judicial functions.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24674.html|title=Article 116A of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-08|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ==== Chapter III: Administrative Tribunals ==== {{see also|International Crimes Tribunal (Bangladesh)}} States that Parliament shall have the power to establish one or more administrative tribunals. === Part VII: Elections === {{see also| Elections in Bangladesh}} Makes provision for the establishment of an [[Bangladesh Election Commission]], chaired by the Chief Election Commissioner.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24677.html|title=Article 118 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prescribes the functions of the Election Commission.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24678.html|title=Article 119 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the procedure for the appointment of staff to the election commission.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24679.html|title=Article 120 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that there is to be a single electoral roll for each constituency.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24680.html|title=Article 121 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies that in order to qualify for registration as a voter, an individual is required to be a citizen of Bangladesh who has attained the age of 18 years.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24681.html|title=Article 122 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the timetable for conducting general elections.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24682.html|title=Article 123 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that Parliament may from time to time pass laws that regulate the delimitation of constituencies, the preparation of electoral rolls, or the holding of elections.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24683.html|title=Article 124 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prohibits courts in the Republic from questioning the validity of electoral law or elections.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24684.html|title=Article 125 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that it is the duty of all executive authorities in the Republic to assist the Election Commission in the discharge of its functions.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24685.html|title=Article 126 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-13|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} === Part VIII: The Comptroller and Auditor General === {{see also|Comptroller and Auditor General (Bangladesh)}} Makes provision for the establishment of a [[Comptroller and Auditor General (Bangladesh)|Comptroller and Auditor General of Bangladesh]].{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24686.html|title=Article 127 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-14|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Prescribes the functions and duties of the Auditor-General.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24687.html|title=Article 128 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-14|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the term of office for the Auditor-General.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24688.html|title=Article 129 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-14|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the procedure for the appointment of an Acting Auditor-General.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24689.html|title=Article 130 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-14|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the Public Accounts of the Republic will be kept in a manner prescribed by the Auditor-General.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24690.html|title=Article 131 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-14|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} States that the reports of the Auditor-General are to be laid before Parliament.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24691.html|title=Article 132 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-14|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} === Part IX: The Services of Bangladesh === ==== Chapter I: Services ==== States that Parliament may by law regulate the appointment of persons employed by the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24692.html|title=133 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-23|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Specifies the tenure in office for persons employed by the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24693.html|title=Article 134 of the Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-23|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Outlines the procedure for the dismissal of persons from service to the Republic.{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24694.html|title=Article 135 of The Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-23|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} Makes provision for the reorganisation of the services of the Republic{{Cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367/section-24695.html|title=Article 136 of The Constitution of Bangladesh|access-date=2021-07-23|publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], [[Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]]}} ** '''Chapter II''':Public Service Commissions * '''Part X''': Amendment of the Constitution * '''Part XI''': Miscellaneous ==Freedom of religion== [[Freedom of religion]] is one of the cornerstones of Bangladesh's Constitution.{{cite web|url=http://www.thepersecution.org/world/bangladesh/2004/10/ds041003law.html |title=Freedom of Religion: religious minority in Bangladesh - The Daily Star, Bangladesh |website=Thepersecution.org |access-date=2017-07-11}} Article 12 calls for [[secularity]], the elimination of interfaith tensions and prohibits the abuse of religion for political purposes and any discrimination against, or persecution of, persons practicing a particular religion.{{cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/sections_detail.php?id=367§ions_id=24560 |title=12. Secularism and freedom of religion |website=Bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd |access-date=2017-07-11}} Article 41 subjects religious freedom to public order, law and morality; it gives every citizen the right to profess, practice or propagate any religion; every religious community or denomination the right to establish, maintain and manage its religious institutions; and states that no person attending any educational institution shall be required to receive religious instruction, or to take part in or to attend any religious ceremony or worship, if that instruction, ceremony or worship relates to a religion other than his own.{{cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/sections_detail.php?id=367§ions_id=24589 |title=41. Freedom of religion |website=Bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd |access-date=2017-07-11}} Governments have generally supported and respected religious freedom.[https://2009-2017.state.gov/documents/organization/171752.pdf United States Department of State] ==International agreements== As of 2017, Bangladesh is a state party to the following international treaties concerning human rights.{{Cite web |url=https://www.unicef.org/bangladesh/Child_Rights_Convention.pdf |title=Conventions and Treaties Ratified by Bangladesh |publisher=UNICEF |access-date=3 July 2017 |archive-date=25 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025093338/http://www.unicef.org/bangladesh/Child_Rights_Convention.pdf |url-status=dead }} Bangladesh can in theory be held liable for its performance in the fields of these treaties. *[[International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights]] *[[International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights]] *[[Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment]] *[[International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination]] *[[Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide]] *[[Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court]] *[[Convention on the Rights of the Child]] *[[Convention on Consent to Marriage, Minimum Age for Marriage and Registration of Marriages]] *[[Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities]] *[[Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women]] *[[Convention on the Political Rights of Women]] Among the notable agreements Bangladesh is not a state party to include the following. *[[Convention relating to the Status of Refugees]] *[[Convention relating to the Status of Stateless Persons]] *[[Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness]] *[[International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance]] *[[Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention]] *[[Second Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights]] on abolishing the death penalty ==Judicial precedent== Article 111 of the Constitution proclaims the doctrine of binding [[judicial precedent]]. According to the article, the law declared by the [[Supreme Court of Bangladesh]], including its Appellate Division and the [[High Court Division]], are binding in all subordinate courts.{{cite web|url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/sections_detail.php?id=367§ions_id=24668 |title=111. Binding effect of Supreme Court judgments |website=Bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd |access-date=2017-07-11}} ==Judicial review== {{Main|Judicial review in Bangladesh}} The Constitution does not specifically mention the term [[judicial review]], but Article 102 allows writ petitions to be filed at the High Court Division for reviewing laws, the actions and policies of authorities and lower court proceedings. Articles 7(2), 26, 44(1) & 102 are considered to indirectly support the system of judicial review.{{Cite web|url=https://bdjls.org/introduction-judicial-review-bangladesh/|title=Constitutional Basis for Judicial Review in Bangladesh|date=2016-08-10|website=Bangladesh Journal of Legal Studies|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-08-15}} ==Constitutional reform== Dr. [[Kamal Hossain]], who is described as the “father of the Bangladeshi Constitution”, has been an ardent supporter of reforming the document to reflect the values of the 21st century.{{cite news |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/forum/2010/November/dreams.htm |title=Forum |newspaper=The Daily Star |access-date=2017-07-11}} Hossain has blamed amendments during military rule for eroding the Constitution's principles. Justice [[Muhammad Habibur Rahman]], a former Chief Justice and interim prime minister, proposed that a Constitution Commission be formed to explore the prospects for Constitutional reform.{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-31148 |title=Military dictating no good for country, armed forces |newspaper=The Daily Star |access-date=2017-07-11}} [[A. T. M. Shamsul Huda]], a former Chief Election Commissioner, has called for a Constitutional amendment to ensure "checks and balances" and the [[separation of powers]].{{cite news |author=Star Online Report |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/politics/Constitutional-reform-healthy-politics%E2%80%99-81493 |title=Constitutional reform for healthy politics |newspaper=The Daily Star |access-date=2017-07-11}} ==Amendments== {{main|Amendments to the Constitution of Bangladesh}} {{As of|2018}}, the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh has been amended 17 times. ==Comparisons with other Constitutions== {| class="wikitable" !Government !Influence |- |{{flagicon|UK}} [[Constitution of the United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] | * [[Westminster system|Parliamentary government]] * Concept of single citizenship * [[Rule of law]] * The [[Speaker of the Lok Sabha|legislative speaker]] and their role * Legislative procedure |- |{{flagicon|USA}} [[United States Constitution|United States]] | * Independent judiciary and separation of powers * Judicial review * President as commander-in-chief of the armed forces * Equal protection under law * Power to declare war reserved for the legislature |- |{{flagicon|IRE}} [[Constitution of Ireland|Ireland]] |Directive principles of state policy |- |{{flagicon|AUS}} [[Constitution of Australia|Australia]] |Preamble terminology |- |{{flagicon|FRA}} [[Constitution of France|France]] |Concepts of ''[[liberté, égalité, fraternité]]'' |- |{{flagicon|SUN}} [[Constitution of the Soviet Union|Soviet Union]] |Fundamental Duties under article 20 |- |{{flagicon|JPN}} [[Constitution of Japan|Japan]] |Due process |} Bangladesh has a single codified document as its Constitution, as in the [[United States Constitution|United States]], [[Constitution of India|India]], [[Constitution of Brazil|Brazil]], [[Constitution of Pakistan|Pakistan]], [[Constitution of Germany|Germany]] and [[Constitution of France|France]]. It is not an [[unwritten constitution]] or a set of Constitutional statutes, as in [[British Constitution|Britain]], [[Constitution of Israel|Israel]], [[Constitution of Canada|Canada]], [[Constitution of New Zealand|New Zealand]], [[Constitution of Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabia]] and [[Constitution of Sweden|Sweden]]. ==See also== *[[List of national constitutions]] ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== * {{cite web |url=http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-367.html |title=The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh |date=2011 |website=Laws of Bangladesh |publisher=[[Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division]], Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs}} * [http://www.bdlawdigest.org/glimpses-on-pre-Constitutional-documents-of-bangladesh/ Glimpses on pre-Constitutional documents of Bangladesh] {{Bangladesh topics}} {{Symbols of Bangladesh}} {{Asia topic|Constitution of|title=Constitutions of Asia|IR=Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Constitution of Bangladesh| ]] [[Category:Government of Bangladesh]]
